name: Centrism
summary: Centrism takes an intermediate, pragmatic position between left and right, preferring moderate policy and practical results to ideological appeals. Its best-documented programmes, the Third Way or New Centre of Blair, Schroeder and the US New Democrats and the radical middle of Satin and of Halstead and Lind, accept a market economy and an active but modernised state, pair rights with responsibilities and favour opportunity over equal outcomes. On most other questions its sources record no common position.
scope: The reference works define centrism as a relational, intermediate and pragmatic position between left and right (s5, s6). This profile reads it through the programmes those works and the Third Way literature tie to it: the Blair-Schroeder Third Way / New Centre paper (1999), the New Democrat agenda as Clinton restated it (the 1990 New Orleans Declaration, 1995 and 2000 remarks), and the radical-middle texts (Satin; Halstead and Lind as reported). It excludes centrist parties as such, centrist populism, and agrarian or Christian-democratic centres, none of which the sources describe as part of the ideology. Where the strands differ (pensions, for example) the answer is mixed.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Halstead and Lind would simplify but retain the income tax, and the Blair-Schroeder paper proposes lower starting rates of income tax for working families.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper and the encyclopedia entry take a market economy for granted, which rests on money and wages.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The New Orleans Declaration says to prevent crime and punish criminals, and Clinton's agenda calls for more police, prevention and prosecutors.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper treats flexible labour markets, including a low-wage sector, as part of a sound economy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says deficit spending cannot cure structural weakness and that high government borrowing must fall, while allowing deficits in a cyclical downturn; Clinton's remarks stress paying down the debt.

basic-income.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says social justice is more than cash transfers and that everyone is expected to take up the work and training offered, which conflicts with an unconditional income.

central-planning.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says heavy-handed state intervention points in the wrong direction and that product, capital and labour markets must all be flexible.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says traditional workplace conflicts must be overcome through partnership and dialogue between all groups, with employees sharing in the rewards of success.

conscription.rationale: Satin's radical-middle book has a chapter calling for bringing back the draft for everyone.

decide-locally.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says problems should be solved where they can best be solved and that power should be devolved to the lowest possible level.

delink-world-market.rationale: Satin's radical-middle account says globalization should be made to work for everyone, and Clinton's New Democrat record lists trade agreements and opening new markets; neither accepts poor countries cutting their ties to rich ones.

democracy-best.rationale: The encyclopedia entry describes the post-Cold War centrist ideology as more supportive of democracy and capitalism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says traditional class conflicts must be overcome through partnership between all groups, the opposite of one class holding dictatorial power.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Clinton's DLC remarks say the aim is to build one America by making a strength of its diversity.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Halstead and Lind, as Kahlenberg reports, would replace race-based preferences with need-based ones, and Satin's book calls for affirmative action for the truly disadvantaged of every race.

equal-conscription.rationale: Satin's radical-middle book calls for a draft for everyone this time, covering women as well as men.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper seeks equal opportunity regardless of race, age or disability, and the New Orleans Declaration backs a politics of inclusion and the protection of civil rights.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says social justice was wrongly confused with equality of outcome and neglected rewarding effort, and sets equality of opportunity as the aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Clinton's DLC remarks call for making a strength of diversity so that other nations can overcome ethnic tensions.

experts-over-public.rationale: Halstead and Lind, as Satin reports, argue that institutions built on expert-led, paternalistic rule now retard progress and design policy around increasing individual choice.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Halstead and Lind, as Kahlenberg reports, would simplify but keep a progressive income tax, and the Blair-Schroeder paper wants lower starting rates within an income tax.

free-trade.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper calls open trade essential to productivity and growth and says the costs of change come before the longer-term gains; the New Orleans Declaration says to expand trade, not restrict it.

future-generations.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper commits to reconcile material progress with environmental sustainability and responsibility to future generations.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Clinton's DLC remarks back national service partly because it lets young people see how different people live and what they share.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Clinton's remarks say emitting more greenhouse gases is no longer needed to grow an economy and call for reversing the course of climate change.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper commends the working families tax credit and lower starting rates of tax to make work pay, and Clinton lists raising the earned-income tax credit among New Democrat priorities.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Halstead and Lind would replace pay-as-you-go Social Security with compulsory savings accounts, while Clinton's agenda extends the life of Social Security and adds retirement accounts beside it; the two strands differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says most people have abandoned the world view of the dogmas of left and right, and the radical-middle statement places the outlook off the traditional left-right spectrum; the encyclopedia defines centrism relative to the spectrum without calling it outdated.

limit-growth.rationale: Clinton argues the economy can grow while the environment improves and that growth need not rise with emissions, and the Blair-Schroeder paper aims to marry environmental responsibility with material progress.

nation-first.rationale: Satin's radical-middle account stresses cosmopolitan world citizenship, and the New Orleans Declaration says the US must stay engaged in the world and not retreat from it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper backs a market economy, not a market society, and sets out a programme of modernising the welfare state within it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says the aim is to modernise the welfare state, not dismantle it, and gives government an active role in education, training and employment.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says social justice requires rewarding effort and responsibility.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper is pro-Europe, says some problems can only be tackled at European level and supports integration where it adds value, while rejecting a European superstate.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The New Orleans Declaration says the US should stay engaged in the struggle for liberty and human rights, and Clinton lists new initiatives to advance democracy abroad.

public-ownership.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says government supports enterprise but is never a substitute for it and that the state should steer, not row, so it does not call for broad public ownership of industry.

racial-franchise.rationale: The New Orleans Declaration backs the protection of civil rights and the inclusion of minorities in the national mainstream, which excludes a vote limited to one ethnic group.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The New Orleans Declaration backs the protection of civil rights and the inclusion of minorities, and the Blair-Schroeder paper seeks equal opportunity regardless of race.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper says companies must not be gagged by rules and regulations and that over-regulation hampers growth.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The encyclopedia entry says a centrist downplays ideological appeals for a pragmatic platform, and the Blair-Schroeder paper wants issues approached without ideological preconceptions and solved by practical, pragmatic policies.

school-vouchers.rationale: Halstead and Lind, as Kahlenberg reports, would let students use government money to attend public or private schools of their choice.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper backs a market economy, not a market society, with a modernised welfare state, and the Satin review reports Halstead and Lind's radical centre also providing a true safety net.

state-as-business.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper tells the public sector to promote efficiency, competition and high performance and to cut bureaucracy.

state-harmful.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper gives the state an active, newly conceived role in jobs, education and public services, which excludes abolishing it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The New Orleans Declaration, as Clinton quotes it, says economic security comes from expanding trade, not restricting it, and the Blair-Schroeder paper says the EU should push for liberalisation of world trade.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper treats taxes as the funding of decent public services and asks fairness towards those who pay them, not as theft.

traditional-family.rationale: Clinton's New Democrat remarks stress the importance of family, and his Georgetown speech says that if every child had both parents contributing there would be almost no poor children.

unions-good.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper supports modern trade unions that protect individuals against arbitrary treatment and work with employers on long-term prosperity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Blair-Schroeder paper expects every unemployed person to take up the jobs and training offered, with rights and responsibilities going together, and Clinton sought welfare law with tough work requirements.

missingStatements.text: Citizens' rights should be matched by responsibilities.
missingStatements.rationale: The Third Way paper and the New Democrat declaration both make rights and responsibilities go together, and no statement in the bank asks this.

quotes.text: Too often rights were elevated above responsibilities, but the responsibility of the individual to his or her family, neighbourhood and society cannot be offloaded on to the state.
We said we believe American citizenship entails responsibility as well as rights, and we mean to ask citizens to give something back to their community.
quotes.where: page 995, quoting the New Orleans Declaration

missingStatements.text: Public programmes should be judged by their results.
missingStatements.rationale: The Third Way paper and Clinton both judge public programmes by results, and no statement in the bank asks this.

quotes.text: The real test for society is how effectively this expenditure is used and how much it enables people to help themselves.
we emphasized results and proven strategies.

notes: Radical-middle texts (Satin; Halstead and Lind as reviewed) are used only where they state a position; Third Way and New Democrat texts carry most answers. Themes searched: economy and taxes, welfare and work, public finance, trade and globalisation, Europe and world affairs, crime, race and civil rights, environment, family, democracy and government, force and conscription, using the Third Way and New Democrat primary texts, the radical-middle texts and the scholarship on them. The sources say little on religion, sex and gender, courts and constitutions, nationalism, technology and animals; those stay null. The two strands differ on pensions and taxes; Satin and Halstead and Lind are the radical middle's own accounts and Kahlenberg's and Satin's reviews report Halstead and Lind's proposals. Britannica and Merriam-Webster refused scripted access and were not used. Giddens's The Third Way (1998) and Halstead and Lind's The Radical Center (2001) were not available as text, so they are cited only through reviews.
